notFound: Ireland prices on the maker's own site: samsung.com/ie lists 94 TV model numbers but prints no price for any of them, so every IE offer (76) comes from DID Electrical's own did.ie collection page (ex-display units skipped); Harvey Norman IE, Currys IE and Argos IE were not read.

Canada: samsung.com/ca lists 231 TV model numbers but its finder feed prices only 114 of them (the regular price, with any sale price separate, and equal to the listing-page figure on the 41 items I compared), so the other 117 CA models have no price; Best Buy Canada answered HTTP 403 and Walmart Canada was not tried.

Retailer pages for the US (Best Buy, Walmart), the UK (Currys, Argos, John Lewis) and Mexico (Liverpool, Coppel, Walmart MX) were not read, because samsung.com/us, /uk and /mx already printed prices for those markets and the fetch budget went to them.

UK and Mexico coverage: samsung.com/uk lists 267 TV model numbers but prices only 99, and samsung.com/mx lists 194 but prices only 58; the unpriced ones (for example QE85QN990HTXXU and the UK 2025 QN80F, S90F and S95F sizes) appear only as regionalModels.

Price source: UK, IE, CA and MX figures (and 16 US SKUs that are not on the family pages) were read from the JSON feeds that samsung.com's own listing and spec pages call (searchapi.samsung.com product finder and spec detail) and from DID's collection JSON rather than from rendered HTML; the 102 US family-page SKUs that also appear in the feed carry identical regular and current prices, and one UK product page (MRE65R85HAUXXU) matches the feed's price and power lines.

EPREL: no EPREL registration number or eprel.ec.europa.eu link appears on Samsung's UK/IE product pages or in the text of the one product fiche PDF I read (QE65S90HAEXXU), because the EPREL QR exists only as an image on the label, so eprel is null for every product.

On-mode watts: 222 products carry Samsung's spec-table 'Power Consumption (Typical)' (the samsung.com/uk figure where a UK model number exists, otherwise the US or CA table) and the 65-inch S90H is confirmed on the UK product fiche as on-mode power SDR 85 W, equal to its spec-table figure; the US table prints much higher typical figures than the UK one for the same set (65-inch S90H: 141 W US, 85 W UK), so powerBasis names which table was used.

No watt figure could be read for 16 products: Samsung Mexico's spec tables print no power lines (U8200H, U8500H), the CA tables for U7900H and U8200F and the US data for MICRO LED MS1B have no typical-power line, and the DID-only listings for the 2024 QN800D 65-inch and LS03D 85-inch have no spec table on any Samsung page I read.

Refresh rates: refreshHz is the first figure on Samsung's spec 'Refresh Rate' line, which is the base rate on 2025 lines ('120Hz (Up to 144Hz)' gives 120) and the headline VRR rate on 2026 lines ('165 Hz (VRR Support)' gives 165; the UK page adds '(100 Hz Native)' while the UK fiche for QE65S90HAEXXU lists a default rate of 165), and UK figures of 50 and 100 Hz are recorded as 60 and 120 because Samsung's UK and US lines for the same models print 50/100 against 60/120; it is null for the Mexico-only U8200H and U8500H and for the 89-inch MICRO LED.

Panel labels: Samsung Micro RGB (R85H, R95H, R95F) has no matching value in the allowed list and is recorded as Mini-LED (an LCD with a micro-sized LED backlight), not MicroLED; Neo QLED (Quantum Mini LED), The Frame Pro and The Terrace are recorded as Mini-LED, plain QLED lines and The Frame as QLED, Samsung's Mini LED M-series as Mini-LED, and the S95-series as OLED because Samsung's pages never say QD-OLED.

Models with no price anywhere I read, so not recorded: The Serif (UK LS01D*, CA LS01D*) and The Sero (CA LS05B) are listed on samsung.com/uk and /ca with no price and are not listed for the US, IE or MX; the US finder also lists suffix-D/B variants (QN70HD, S90HD, S85HD, M70HB, M70HD, M80HD) with no price, and lists 2025 U7900F (43 to 85 inch), Q6F (75 and 85 inch), Q8FD (75 inch), DU9000 (98 inch) and 2024 QE1D, DUX1E and S90D (77 inch) SKUs with no price whose family pages I did not fetch, so any out-of-stock page price for them was not read.

The Movingstyle 27-inch QHD portable screen (UE27LSM7FAXXXU at GBP 999 on samsung.com/uk and EUR 1,199.99 at DID, UN27LSM7FAXXZC in Canada) was left out because QHD is not in the allowed resolution list.

Availability: samsung.com marks 69 of the 162 US offers (59 on the 2025 family pages plus 10 older or 2025 SKUs from the finder, e.g. S85F, S90F, S95F, QN90F, Q8F, U8000F), 25 of the 111 CA offers and 13 of the 58 MX offers as out of stock (10 more MX are pre-order) and 3 DID listings are unavailable, so I could not confirm those can still be bought; the printed regular price is what is recorded.

Samsung Canada lists a typo twin SKU for each 2026 U7900H size (UN55U790MHFXZC, UN65U790MHFXZC, UN75U790MHFXZC) at the same price as the correctly spelled UN55U7900HFXZC, UN65U7900HFXZC and UN75U7900HFXZC, so only the correctly spelled model number is recorded for each size.

The model year of the MICRO LED MS1B (89 and 101 inch, USD 109,999 and 129,999.99) is not stated in the samsung.com/us finder or spec data, so year is null; the retailer-variant series S83H, S93H, S99H, M72H, QN73H and LS03HA (UK) and S88H, S92H, M82H, M1EH and QN82H (CA) are recorded as their own products because each has its own model number and page.
